# AI coding research brief — October 9, 2026

Historical backfill published October 17, 2026. Reconstructed from recovered prior-conversation findings; this is not a verbatim transcript. The original selections, reported results, caveats, and proposed experiments are preserved in condensed form. Dates below are publication dates recorded in the original brief. These are research proposals, not demonstrated Quadratus improvements or implementation instructions.

## 1. When Sub-Agents Work in Parallel: The Promises and Pitfalls of Dynamic Concurrency in Long-Horizon Coding Tasks
**October 7, 2026 · [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.10263)**

Across 354 tasks and 2,124 executions, dynamic concurrency helped some long-horizon tasks with complementary work, but offered little or negative benefit on bounded repair. It consumed 1.41–3.31 times as many tokens. The study identifies 13 failure subcategories and 28 observable patterns.

**Why read it and limitations:** Delegation needs an admission rule tied to useful parallel work. Native model and harness differences are intertwined, and long-horizon benchmarks are sampled. Parallelism did not generally lower end-to-end runtime.

**Proposed Quadratus experiment:** Default to one worker for bounded repairs. Admit concurrent workers for separable tasks, alternative exploration or independent verification, and reserve 25–30% of the budget for integration and testing. That reservation is a proposed heuristic, not a validated optimum.

## 2. StateWise: Diagnosing and Repairing Persistent Operational State Before Agent Actions
**October 4, 2026 · [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.05241)**

StateWise identifies action-critical stored records, checks current validity, repairs persistent state with scoped evidence, and replans before execution. On 150 corrupted-state cases, it reported 93.3% correctness versus 38.7% for the baseline, with no unsafe actions observed. The earlier brief also reported 92.7% subsequent completion across 32 four-task sequences.

**Why read it and limitations:** A coordinator can repeatedly reuse a stale assumption even when individual actions are reviewed. The cases are designed/research-informed and center on one primary planner; observed safety in this set is not a general guarantee.

**Proposed Quadratus experiment:** Trace which stored facts support each action. Revalidate machine-observable claims, distinguish developer-owned intent, and replace invalid records with scoped, evidence-linked corrections.

## 3. What Does a Harness Buy? Tokens, Mostly
**October 3, 2026 · [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.04433)**

On a hard subset, changing harnesses flipped about 13% of task outcomes—the same rate as rerunning an unchanged harness. With the same model and price list, cost varied by up to threefold. Repeated prompt and tool-schema overhead explained much of the difference.

**Why read it and limitations:** Small score gains may be run noise while cost differences are real. The large comparison used only two models on one benchmark; a 45-task subset cannot reliably establish modest gains.

**Proposed Quadratus experiment:** Require repeated runs and uncertainty intervals. Record preamble/tool-schema tokens, worker calls and total cost separately. Treat small gains as unproven until the evaluation has adequate power.

## 4. Harness Engineering for Software Engineering via Modular Executable Dev-Primitives
**October 6, 2026 · [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.07832)**

HERMES assigns repository components agent interfaces, activates them through dependencies, and maps failure evidence back to the components needing changes. It reports a 12.4-percentage-point average improvement across four benchmarks. Qwen3-8B local components with stronger activation/diagnosis models reduced Terminal-Bench inference cost by 26.2% versus the homogeneous configuration.

**Why read it and limitations:** Component ownership may help bound context and route debugging. Some comparisons rely on published baselines, coordination adds cost, and choosing component boundaries remains a practical uncertainty. These results do not establish gains for Quadratus.

**Proposed Quadratus experiment:** Prototype one subsystem with workers owning tightly coupled components, tests and dependency summaries. Route interface changes to affected neighbors and reactivate owners implicated by failures.

## 5. Agent Skill Evolution: How Revisions Affect Coding Agents
**October 4, 2026 · [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.04832)**

Across four agents, adding checkable rules increased the required-action rate by 0.23 on average; blind-judged final correctness increased by 0.10 across three assessed agents. Normal selective loading retained only part of the action gain.

**Why read it and limitations:** Skills can be versioned and evaluated as behavioral dependencies. The agent evaluation is small, artifact-check agreement is imperfect, and the study focuses on checkable rules rather than all forms of guidance.

**Proposed Quadratus experiment:** Version specialist skills like code and add regression probes for required commands, files and gates. Compare forced loading with normal retrieval to separate skill quality from activation failures.

## The single most promising idea to try

Add a concurrency admission controller: one worker by default for bounded repairs, with extra workers admitted for separable work, alternative exploration or independent verification. Reserve integration/testing capacity and compare against unconditional fan-out on success, wall time, tokens, merge failures and incomplete integrations.
